name: The noise (reels pile up behind you)
what: Your reels pile up on the wall behind your head, one every quarter second, each at its own slight angle and spot around you with a soft shadow, until the wall is busy; each lands with a small overshoot and settles, the pile drifts a hair while it grows, and it clears away at the end. Every reel shows its cover, a play mark and a view count. The Editor puts it behind you and moves it with the camera.
origin: MotionLab's own build after a design in Vibha Ramprakash's claude-video-effects (MIT), 2026-10-28
motion: from f1 a reel lands every 7 f (about a quarter second; 15 reels in 4 s, 4 to 16 by the length): each scales from 60 % with a small overshoot (8 f, decelerating with overshoot), fades in over 2-3 f and turns 5-9 degrees into its own slight angle; once landed each drifts 2-3 px and 0.5 degree (a slow sine, out of step); the last 12 f the pile clears, the newest first, 0.3 f apart: each shrinks 12 %, sinks 14 px and fades in 7 f (accelerating)

tracks.name: reels land
tracks.what: a reel lands every 7 frames with a small overshoot and a settling turn

tracks.name: drift
tracks.what: the landed reels drift a hair, out of step

tracks.name: clear
tracks.what: the pile clears away, the newest first

min_why: at least four reels have to land before the pile clears
